notes: Machine-readable policy table. Loaded by src/fhir_sulo/identity.
No entry here asserts owl:sameAs between a FHIR resource and a person.
A resolved FHIR reference is lineage, not a person-equivalence claim.

key_style_options.scoped-hash: person-<32 lowercase hex chars>. Source-scoped by construction; two sources that both hold Patient/p123 get different IRIs. Safe default.
key_style_options.legacy-concept-note: person-<resource-id-slug>, matching the concept note's ex:person-p123. ONLY valid when entity_iri.single_source_scope is set; a request from any other scope is rejected, not silently keyed.

entity_iri.key_revision_note: Deliberately NOT the table's semantic version. Entity IRIs are stable across every policy edit that does not change the keying answer; bumping this revision is an explicit, breaking re-keying decision that needs a DR-4xx record. Agent 6 can therefore treat an entity IRI as stable while identity-policy.version moves.
entity_iri.key_input_normalisation: Unicode NFC, then canonical JSON (sorted keys, no whitespace, ASCII-escaped), then sha256. No timestamps, no process state, no Python hash().

reference_scope.rationale: Concept note section 2 and plan section 7: never merge two references into one person without recorded evidence.
reference_scope.accepted_merge_evidence_note: Empty on purpose. No cross-source merge rule has been reviewed, so no cross-source merge can occur. Adding an entry here is a reviewed decision, not an implementation detail.

resolution_rules.when: Exactly one candidate whose resolved_resource_type is in the request's expected_resource_types.
Zero candidates supplied by reference resolution.
More than one candidate and they do not all agree on (source_scope_id, resource_type, resource_id).
More than one candidate and all agree on (source_scope_id, resource_type, resource_id).
resolution_rules.note: Not a merge across identities: it is the same triple of key inputs observed more than once.

resolution_rules.when: A candidate's resource_type is not in expected_resource_types.
A required key input field is absent or empty after normalisation.
key_style is legacy-concept-note and the candidate's source_scope_id differs from entity_iri.single_source_scope.
resolution_rules.note: Guards the readable key style against the exact failure it invites.

ambiguity.api_contract: Rejection is a distinct return type with no entity IRI attribute. There is no Optional-IRI return anywhere in the identity API.

quality_identity.mode_status: SET (provisional) - reviewer answered R2 = B on 2026-09-30. Explicitly not settled; see reviewer_decision.revisit.
quality_identity.key_revision_note: As for entity_iri.key_revision: quality IRIs are stable across policy edits that do not change the keying answer. Note that CHANGING quality_identity.mode does change every quality IRI, unavoidably, because the two modes key on different inputs. That is a graph-key-affecting decision, not an incidental version bump.
quality_identity.unset_behaviour_note: While mode is null every quality-identity request returns a rejection with reason_code quality-identity-policy-unset. Nothing downstream can accidentally ship a guessed policy.

persistent-per-person-code.description: One persisting quality entity per (person, observable code). The same renal-filtration quality IRI is reused across every eGFR observation for that person.
persistent-per-person-code.implication: Independent records about the same person and code converge on one quality node. Matches the concept note's ex:renal-quality-p123 example graph.
persistent-per-person-code.risk: Two records the project does not actually intend to be about one persisting quality will merge.

per-observation.description: A quality entity keyed by person, observable code, the source observation version, and the clinically relevant time.
per-observation.implication: Independent records never merge unknowingly (concept note section 4).
per-observation.risk: A query for 'the patient's renal filtration quality' returns many distinct nodes; cross-observation trend queries must join on the code rather than on the quality IRI.

quality_identity.reviewer_question: Does a quality IRI persist across observations for a patient (persistent-per-person-code), or is it keyed per observation plus time plus code (per-observation)? Concept note section 4 and plan Gate 0 both flag this as a reviewer decision. Both behaviours are implemented; the default is deliberately unset and rejects.

reviewer_decision.status: provisional - the underlying question is NOT resolved
reviewer_decision.reviewer_words: Whether there is a single quality of a particular kind for an individual, or whether there can be multiple distinct instances, is not yet resolved. One per event with its associated value is probably safest. This needs revisiting in a coherent theory, compared against other upper-level ontologies.
reviewer_decision.consequence_measured: Under per-observation a correction (v1 to v2) mints a NEW quality node while the quantity keeps its IRI, so a correction is visible in the graph's identity. Under persistent-per-person-code it would not be.
reviewer_decision.revisit: Reconcile quality individuation against other ULOs before clinical use. Both modes remain implemented and tested; switching re-keys every quality IRI and is a graph migration, not a configuration change.
